title: The White Snake variant

full_text:
A wise king was renowned throughout the world because no secret remained hidden from him. Every evening at supper, after all dishes had been cleared, a trusted servant brought him a covered silver dish, which the king ate alone in absolute secrecy.

Overcome by curiosity, the servant carried the dish to a private room and lifted the lid. Inside lay a cooked white snake. Unable to resist, the servant took a single small bite. Instantly, he understood the speech of all living creatures: birds singing in the boughs, fish whispering beneath the waves, and ants murmuring in the moss!

Armed with this miraculous gift, the servant journeyed across the realm. Along the way, he saved three dying fish by tossing them back into the brook, spared the life of an ant king by steering his horse around an anthill, and fed starving ravens by giving them his own bread.

Arriving at the capital, he sought to win the hand of the king's daughter. The princess set three impossible tasks: to retrieve a golden ring cast into the deep ocean, to gather thousands of spilled millet seeds from the grass before sunrise, and to fetch the golden apple from the Tree of Life.

The grateful fish dived to the ocean floor and retrieved the ring; the thankful ants gathered every single millet seed; and the loyal ravens flew to the edge of the world to bring the golden apple. The amazed princess accepted his hand, and the compassionate youth became king, ruling in wisdom and harmony with all living things.
moral: Compassion extended to creatures of the earth, air, and water returns as a shield in time of need.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The White Snake variant"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
